newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCC rates firm, good Japanese demand seen.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCC rates firm, good Japanese demand seen.

text.p: Very large crude carriers (VLCCs) to most destinations edged up on Thursday on a shortage of tonnage, with some brokers expecting continued tightness on good Japanese demand.
VLCCs from the Middle East to Japan to W65 from W62.5 on Wednesday, with vessels to Singapore up slightly at about W50-52.5 and to the west at W51.5, or slightly higher for modern tonnage.
"It looks like there will be a shortage of ships over the next 30 days. We are expecting Japan to be fairly busy in March and rates to firm in consequence," one broker said.
He said VLCCs from West Africa to the U.S. Gulf also firmed to W67.5 from W62.5 on a lack of available tonnage, with transatlantic VLCCs edging up to W65 in sympathy.
But 130,000 tonne vessels on West Africa/U.S. trips slipped to W90 from W95. "There are not that many ships but most vessels for this month have already been done," another broker said.
Mediterranean rates, which soared for 80,000 tonners in late January to as high as W170, were steady at W130/135. Med 130,000 tonne vessels were also steady at W90/95.
Inter-U.K./Cont rates for 80,000 tonne ships were steady to slightly weaker at W95/100. "I think it could drop a couple of more points. There's plenty of tonnage around," one broker said.
Fuel oil was quiet and rates were unchanged, with 25,000 tonnes inter-U.K./Cont at W210 and cross-Med at W190.
In the Caribbean, 70,000 tonne crude cargoes fell to W135 from W145, with 50,000 tonne fuel cargoes at W165 from W170.
Referring to crude, one broker said, "There are a lot of ships and not as many cargoes, and also a lot of re-lets." He noted that fuel oil has fallen 20 points in the last two weeks.
